summary:
POLLE is an end-to-end Decision Support System solving the "Field Shift" challenge by bridging NASA Earth observations with daily farm operations.

It acts as a Farm Digital Twin, harmonizing multi-resolution spatial datasets—NASA GIBS (SMAP, MODIS), NASA POWER, and NOAA drought trends—into an interactive map. Built for global scalability, POLLE relies on borderless Earth observations and universal FAO biophysical standards, working just as effectively for a farm in Ukraine or Kenya as in the American Midwest. These climate projections and soil profiles feed directly into the Math-Bees Solver, our custom biophysical and CP-SAT optimization engine.

Math-Bees empowers farmers to stress-test existing crop schedules or generate highly optimized 10-year rotation strategies. It evaluates millions of permutations across 200 priority configurations—tracking root-zone moisture, NPK nutrient cycling, and pest-disrupting return intervals—while strictly enforcing real-world budget, machinery, and labor constraints.

Paired with a deterministic, hallucination-free SI Assistant, POLLE translates deep agronomic science into clear Gantt timelines and risk audits. It delivers a transparent, human-in-the-loop co-pilot that helps farmers conserve water, restore soil health, and secure profitability without overriding their local expertise.
details:
Overview & How It Works

The POLLE Platform & Farm Digital Twin

POLLE is a decision-support co-pilot solving the "Field Shift" challenge by bridging global NASA Earth observations with daily farm realities. Designed to help farmers adapt to changing climates, it empowers them to generate and compare climate-resilient crop rotations that restore soil health, conserve water, and maintain profitability. Operating as a Farm Digital Twin, POLLE harmonizes multi-resolution spatial datasets—NASA GIBS (SMAP, MODIS) and NASA POWER—into an interactive map. These projections feed into the Math-Bees Solver, a custom biophysical and CP-SAT optimization engine. The system evaluates millions of permutations, tracking root-zone moisture, NPK nutrient cycling, and pest-disrupting intervals, while strictly enforcing real-world constraints. Paired with a deterministic SI Assistant, POLLE acts as a transparent human-in-the-loop tool that supports—but never overrides—local agricultural expertise.

  • Interactive Field Mapping & Live Satellite Overlays: Farmers draw exact field and subfield boundaries directly over high-resolution Esri World Imagery or OpenStreetMap layers using a vector editor with magnetic vertex snapping and self-intersection blocking. Crucially, farmers can toggle NASA satellite layers (NDVI, SMAP soil moisture, land surface temperature) and drought projections directly on the same map while outlining plots—identifying water-stressed zones or vulnerable areas in context without switching tools. Boundaries are stored as WGS84 GeoJSON polygons with PostGIS-computed areas and strict non-overlap checks.
  • Multi-Year Crop Plans & Decadal Scheduling: Farmers maintain a live multi-year planting timeline (past, active, and planned crops) via a decadal calendar aligned with the solver's 1st, 11th, and 21st monthly sowing windows. Overlapping crop intervals on the same plot are strictly blocked at the database level via PostgreSQL GiST exclusion constraints, guaranteeing a valid temporal baseline.
  • Farm Budget, Machinery & Labor Control: The Resources & Finance workspace tracks total farm budgets across eight expense categories (seeds, fertilizers, crop protection, fuel, machinery, labor, irrigation, and other), logs actual versus planned expenses, and monitors machinery hour limits and weekly worker shift schedules. These operational records serve as real-world feasibility constraints when auditing scenario readiness or comparing rotation strategies.
  • Soil Profile Estimation & Land Masking: Rather than fabricating lab tests, farmers input known baseline metrics (texture, drainage, initial NPK reserves), while remaining physicochemical properties are deterministically estimated from a ~5 km spatial grid so neighboring fields share consistent profiles. Fields drawn over marine waters are automatically rejected using a Natural Earth 1:50m land mask.
  • Strategy Orchestration: Farmers can immediately evaluate the risks and economics of their existing planting schedule (Evaluate my plan) or launch up to 12 optimization scenarios at once (Suggest plans, defaulting to six solver presets). The platform renders solver outputs as visual Gantt timelines and risk cards for side-by-side comparison without altering the underlying financial or agronomic figures.

Drilling into any generated plan (such as the Medium preset compared against a farmer's current plan) opens a full diagnostic comparison view designed to make every solver trade-off transparent before adoption:

  • Side-by-Side Gantt Timelines & Plain-Language Diffs: Parallel rotation timelines contrast the proposed crop sequence against the farmer's baseline schedule, paired with an automated year-by-year summary ("What changes") that clearly explains crop substitutions and deliberate soil-rest periods.
  • Monthly Climatic Water Balance: A 60-month hydro-agronomic chart tracks monthly water inflows—combining 10-year averaged NASA POWER precipitation with scheduled irrigation—against actual crop evapotranspiration demand (in mm and field-scaled m³), while shading bare-field intervals ("No crop on the field") to visualize off-season moisture exposure.
  • Itemized Unit Economics & Input Procurement: Each crop cycle details exact sowing, harvest, and field-clearance dates alongside projected revenue, net profit, cost breakdowns (machinery and labor, seed, water, fertilizer), and actionable area-scaled fertilizer purchase quantities (such as exact tonnage of Nitrophoska or Ammonium chloride).
  • Granular Risk & Warning Audit: Rather than hiding model limitations, every crop card surfaces specific solver-detected alerts—including soil pH mismatches, partial nutrient-deficit caps, thermal stage timeouts, and frost-shock yield penalties—giving farmers and local agronomists full visibility into localized risks before manually clicking "Use this plan".

Climate Intelligence & Geospatial Data Fusion

To help farmers explore crop-rotation options that strengthen resilience to changing weather and water conditions, POLLE harmonizes datasets with completely different spatial and temporal resolutions (from 50 km climate cells to 9 km SMAP pixels and sub-meter field boundaries) into a common analysis grid.

  • 0.5° Climate Model & Trend Projections: An offline Python pipeline processes multi-year NOAA CPC daily precipitation and temperature records into a highly compact binary model across 62,876 land cells. It stores 2016–2025 normals and 10-year linear trends, allowing the platform to project expected climate trajectories for 2026–2035 on the fly. To prevent short-term anomalies from causing unrealistic extrapolations, temperature slopes are strictly clamped to ±0.1 °C/year.
  • Evapotranspiration & Drought Classification: Reference evapotranspiration (ET0) is calculated using the FAO-56 Hargreaves equation to compute a 30-day climatic water balance (Precipitation - ET0). This balance is ranked against 1991–2020 seasonal quantiles to classify drought severity (D0–D4) following the US Drought Monitor scale.
  • NASA Earth Observations & Pixel Decoding: We specifically selected SMAP to track root-zone soil moisture—critical for identifying drought vulnerabilities—and MODIS for real-time vegetation stress (NDVI) and surface temperature monitoring. Together with NASA POWER's long-term climate series, these datasets provide the exact inputs needed for accurate FAO-56 biophysical modeling. The interactive map overlays live NASA GIBS WMTS tiles—MODIS Terra NDVI, SMAP L4 root-zone soil moisture, and MODIS Terra Land Surface Temperature. Because GIBS serves imagery rather than raw numerical matrices, the client dynamically calculates Web Mercator coordinates, samples pixel RGB values via HTML5 Canvas, and translates colors back into exact physical units using NASA GIBS Color Maps API v1.3 XML legends.
  • Geospatial Data Harmonization & Field-Level Extraction: The platform visually unifies diverse map layers into a single interface—including NOAA temperature and precipitation trends, NASA GIBS satellite data (Earth's surface, soil moisture, and NDVI), Copernicus EDO, and the internal Polle drought water balance model. For field-specific solver optimizations, the platform retrieves multi-year daily temperature and precipitation series from NASA POWER over the planning horizon, extracted from the corresponding climate grid cell using an interior point of the farmer's drawn polygon.

The Math-Bees Solver

The Math-Bees Solver is POLLE's dedicated Python biophysical and combinatorial optimization service. Built as an explainable decision-support co-pilot, it pairs multi-year climate projections and Earth observations with crop biology and local agronomic expertise to evaluate existing farm plans and generate risk-scored rotation strategies.

Purpose & Operating Modes

By combining multi-source Earth observations with field-specific soil records, it enables side-by-side comparison of a farm's baseline rotation against multiple optimized alternatives across two core modes:

  • Evaluation & Stress-Testing Mode: Simulates a farmer's existing or proposed schedule against multi-year climate projections to pinpoint moisture deficits, thermal shocks, NPK depletion, salinity penalties, and rotation violations while flagging information gaps for on-farm review.
  • Optimization & Strategy Generation Mode: Automatically generates, simulates, and ranks alternative multi-year crop sequences (annuals, perennials) tailored to farm priorities across a 200-configuration execution matrix.
Inputs & Biophysical Simulation Pipeline

The solver integrates field soil profiles (texture, drainage, pH, salinity, initial moisture/NPK reserves), multi-year daily climate series from internal climate API (uses NASA POWER), and curated crop profiles standardized around FAO-56, FAO-33, and FAO-29. Rather than a monolithic loop, the engine runs a composable functional pipeline (map–filter–flatMap) in two modes—fail-fast pruning for optimization and a non-aborting diagnostic audit for baseline evaluation—across five stages:

  1. Rotation & Soil Compatibility: Validates minimum return intervals against planting history, soil texture/drainage/pH bounds, and FAO-29 Maas–Hoffman salinity penalties.
  2. Vectorized Phenology (GDD & Vernalization): Drives crop stage progression (including perennial dormancy and regrowth) via NumPy-vectorized Growing Degree Days (GDD), Vernalization Days (VD), and heat-induced devernalization.
  3. Numba JIT FAO-56 Water Bucket & FAO-33 Stress: Simulates daily root-zone moisture bounded by Total Available Water (TAW), triggers irrigation below Readily Available Water (TAW - RAW), tracks severe water stress days (Ks < 0.4), and quantifies stage yield penalties via FAO-33.
  4. Thermal Shocks, NPK Balance & Liebig's Law: Evaluates frost/heat shock durations, balances target N/P/K uptake against soil fertility and fertilizer-suppressed biological nitrogen fixation (BNF), flags nutrient deficits or soil pH shifts, and resolves yield via Liebig's Law of the Minimum.
  5. Unit Economics & Multi-Year Carryover: Evaluates variable costs against projected revenue. During optimization, unprofitable crops are pruned unless they are perennials, maintain a positive nitrogen balance, or have received fertilizer applications. Continuous bare-field (fallow) dynamics track soil evaporation and natural NPK recovery between crops, followed by an end-to-end carryover audit. To actively promote long-term soil health, the solver evaluates opportunities to introduce nitrogen-fixing plants during these prolonged bare-field periods. This strategic addition helps reduce erosion risks, improves soil organic matter, and supports sustainable nutrient cycling without disrupting the main commercial rotation.
Graceful Degradation & The 200-Configuration Matrix
  • Explicit Information-Gap Audit: On incomplete records, fallback-tolerant mode applies documented biophysical and nearest-year pricing defaults while emitting structured DATA_MISSING notes (INFO, WARN, RISK) so farmers see exactly where assumptions were made.
  • 200-Configuration Matrix (2 x 2 x 2 x 5 x 5): Parameterizes both simulation and optimization across Missing-Data Policy (Strict vs. Fallback-Tolerant), Agronomic Risk Tolerance (Conservative vs. Risk-Tolerant), Soil Depletion Policy (Depletion-Allowed vs. Resource-Preserving, enforcing >=50% mid-horizon and >=100% terminal NPK reserves), 5 Irrigation granularity modes (disabled, or 2, 3, 4, and 6 evaluation levels), and 5 Fertilization granularity modes (disabled, or 2, 3, 4, and 6 evaluation levels).
CP-SAT Optimization, Outputs & Decade-Scale Performance
  • Constraint Programming (Google OR-Tools CP-SAT): Assembles globally optimal schedules from simulated candidates by enforcing exact field exclusivity, pest-disrupting return intervals, monthly water/NPK balance bounds, and multi-year net profit maximization.
  • Extensible Farm-Wide Optimization (L0 → L1 Roadmap): Built with a decoupled, phase-based architecture designed to scale from single-field planning (L0, enforcing local agronomic, soil, and water/NPK balances) to a second-tier global solver (L1). By ingesting the pruned, valid candidate schedules generated at L0 across all farm plots, the L1 layer will jointly optimize shared farm-level resource limits—such as total machinery hours, seasonal labor shifts, and farm-wide budgets—without re-running daily biophysical simulations.
  • Unified Strategy Outputs: Returns chronological crop cycles with exact sowing/harvest dates, yield multipliers, monthly water and NPK trajectories, fertilizer recommendations, itemized unit economics, and categorized risk notes for side-by-side comparison.
  • Decade-Scale Performance: Evaluating 20 crop profiles across a 10-year horizon (360 decadal sowing windows) creates over 10468 theoretical permutations—and tens of thousands of overlapping candidate intervals across resource tiers and daily simulation resolution (3,650 days). Because the Numba JIT pipeline fail-fast prunes non-viable trajectories before passing a compact candidate pool to CP-SAT, a full 10-year single-field optimization benchmarks at 1–3 minutes on standard workstation hardware—keeping cloud compute footprints lean and cost-effective when scaling horizontally across multi-field farms and concurrent users.

The Agronomic SI Assistant

Directly addressing the need for a Farmer-Centered Design, POLLE pairs its intuitive visual workspace with a conversational SI assistant. This ensures the platform remains highly accessible, even for users with limited technical or geospatial experience, by offering farmers a fast way to query farm records, audit data readiness, and compare rotation scenarios in natural language. Its core architectural principle is strict separation between language understanding and computation: the LLM only classifies user intent and extracts entity names, while deterministic C# backend services execute all database queries, date parsing, solver orchestration, and calculations. The model never generates SQL or computes yields or profit—every figure presented to the farmer comes directly from Math-Bees Solver outputs, ensuring absolute accuracy and trust.

Model Stack & MCP Integration
  • Local-First & Provider-Agnostic Inference: Runs Qwen3 4B locally via Ollama (temperature = 0, strict JSON Schema structured outputs) with seamless configuration switching to any OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API.
  • Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server: Exposes the exact same read-only agronomic tools via an official C# SDK MCP server for external agentic clients, enforcing authentication, closed-world read-only execution, and strict input schema validation.
Three-Stage Deterministic Pipeline

Rather than open-ended agent loops, every incoming message traverses a controlled three-stage pipeline:

  • Stage 0 — Zero-LLM Fast Routing: Multilingual regex rules (Ukrainian and English) intercept direct requests about field rotation strategies and short horizon follow-ups (e.g., "10" or "2026-10"), routing them straight to the active tool without invoking the LLM.
  • Stage 1 — Stateful JSON-Schema Classification: Remaining queries are classified against a closed, state-aware JSON Schema enum (ten core actions plus five scenario-inspection actions enabled only when a prepared scenario exists in the dialogue state).
  • Stage 2 — Deterministic C# Orchestrator: The backend verifies state permissions, matches farm or field names strictly against the user's owned PostGIS records (asking for clarification if ambiguous), and resolves natural-language planning periods (defaulting to the next month over a 5-year horizon while explicitly stating assumed dates).
Agronomic Tools & Solver Integration
  • Farm & Field Inspection: Retrieves the user's farms, budgets, PostGIS-computed field areas, and chronological planting/harvest histories.
  • Scenario Readiness Audit: Assembles a read-only solver input draft over a 1–20 year horizon without launching a calculation, returning a ready or incomplete status with an itemized checklist of missing inputs (e.g., budget, field climate series, or machinery/labor hours) and optional JSON export.
  • End-to-End Strategy Comparison: Resolves the target field and horizon, reuses existing calculations for identical periods unless recalculation is requested, or triggers the same workflow as the UI "Suggest plans" button—running six baseline presets plus the farmer's current plan after verifying soil data (land-mask check) and solver health.
  • Weather- & Plan-Aware Hybrid Advisory: Cross-references 12-month field climate projections (drought-risk severity and warm-season climatic water balance) with crops scheduled in a field's active or recommended rotation plan to deterministically rank climate-adapted seed hybrids by drought/heat tolerance and maturity group.
  • Grounded Q&A & Fixed Templates: General agronomic questions pass through a constrained schema with an initial in_scope check and strict anti-fabrication rules, while greetings, capability summaries, and off-topic refusals use static backend templates.
Safety & Human-in-the-Loop Governance
  • Prompt-Injection Defense & Context Isolation: Because the LLM only selects from a closed action enum and never emits tool arguments, IDs, or code, prompt injection and arbitrary execution are structurally blocked. Browser chat history is bounded in length, restricted to user/assistant roles, and treated strictly as untrusted context.
  • Session-Bound Ownership & Non-Destructive Control: Every database query is filtered by the authenticated user's session identity, raw user prompts are never logged, and assistant tools remain non-destructive—promoting any recommended plan into an active rotation plan requires the farmer to review the trade-offs and manually click "Use this plan" in the interface.


As shown in the interface screenshots, a farmer can select Field 2 directly on the map and ask in plain language—"Analyze my field for 5 years."—prompting the deterministic orchestrator to automatically resolve the planning window (2026-12 to 2031-11) and run all six solver presets (Ready: 6 of 6). The assistant immediately returns a transparent breakdown of net profit ($111,473 for Full inputs vs. $101,263 for Medium), costs, irrigation volumes (in mm and m³), crop sequences (Perilla – Industrial hemp – Perilla – Industrial hemp), unfeasible presets (Control, Rainfed potential), and specific phenological stage-duration risks, linked directly to the field's "Plan & suggestions" cards for manual approval. In a stateful follow-up—"Provide me hybrids for Full inputs"—the assistant scopes recommendations directly to the suggested rotation plan ("Hybrids for suggested plan (Field 2)"), cross-referencing its scheduled crops against Field 2's 12-month drought outlook and warm-season water balance (-409 mm) to prioritize adapted varieties (such as Aojiso green shiso perilla suited to irrigated forest-steppe conditions).

Vision & Impact

Ultimately, POLLE translates complex NASA Earth observations... into an accessible, farmer-first workspace. By creating a globally scalable, location-agnostic solver, we are democratizing precision agriculture. It bridges the gap between global climate models and daily farm operations, empowering farmers anywhere in the world to build climate-resilient, profitable crop rotations without ever overriding their invaluable local expertise.
